newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Leader of Portuguese opposition party quits.
newsitem.headline: Leader of Portuguese opposition party quits.

text.p: The leader of Portugal's rightwing opposition Popular Party (PP), Manuel Monteiro, resigned on Tuesday amid a crisis within his party and called an extraordinary congress to elect his successor.
"I am not abandoning politics," Monteiro, whose PP holds 15 seats in the 230-seat parliament, told reporters.
"I am leaving the presidency of the PP to defend my party because I love my party," he added.

The PP which is unenthusiastic about European integration is the third largest party in parliament after the ruling Socialists, who have 112 seats, and the centre-right opposition Social Democratic Party (PSD) who have 88.
The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, elected for a four-year term last October, has a clear majority in parliament but is four seats short of an absolute majority.

Monteiro's resignation came a day after the only candidate in an election for the leadership of the party's parliamentary group, Paulo Portas, withdrew his candidacy after eight of his colleagues abstained and only seven voted for him.
Five Popular Party MPs, including Portas, later suspended their parliamentary mandates to protest against the lack of solidarity within the party for his candidacy.
"I understand that what has happened lately has clearly harmed the party," Monteiro told Channel One state television.

He did not give a date for his party's extraordinary congress, but said it should take place after October 13 when regional elections on Portugal's semi-autonomous islands of Madeira and the Azores are due to take place.
